messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Customer Cygnus (dedicated pool eu-west-1) p99 latency SLO breach. p99 observed 4.6s (SLO 1.2s) over last 5m. Auto-paging oncall.
ops-oncall-ryan: acked — creating warroom. tagging @sre, @eng, @cs. https://redwood.internal/warroom/7165432100 :clipboard:
sre-ryan: quick snapshot: p95 ~ 250ms, p99 spike on tail. High KV cache miss rate for tenant `cygnus-prod-ten1`. Pool nodes CPU ~85-92% on a subset of allocs. suspect tenant noise causing eviction churn.
eng-aya: looking at runtime. seeing long sequence lengths (avg seq 1200 tokens) from that tenant causing KV cache churn + repeated rewarming. suggests isolating tenant to warm spare + temporary rate-limit.
infra-zoe: I can spin a warm spare in ~3-5m in eu-west-1. will prep command; need approval to allocate reserved nodes.
cs-emily: Cygnus CS -> they report ~25% request timeouts on /v1/payments and higher user retries. customer-facing SLA impacted. POC asking for ETA and whether any data lost.
ops-oncall-ryan: proposed mitigation plan (short): 1) enable tenant rate limit 50qps; 2) move tenant to warm-spare pool; 3) scale pool +2 nodes; 4) temporary model-variant fallback for that tenant. asking eng/infra to action now.
eng-aya: executing throttle + model fallback now.
eng-aya: command: `rictl tenant update --tenant cygnus-prod-ten1 --rate-limit 50` ; then `rictl rollout model-variant --tenant cygnus-prod-ten1 --variant rwd-gpt-lite --priority emergency`
eng-aya: note: fallback reduces latency but may drop output quality. will monitor regression dashboard and post any failures.
infra-zoe: warm spare ready -> `rictl pool create --region eu-west-1 --type warm-spare --size 4gpus --label cygnus-spare` completed. initiating tenant move.
infra-zoe: moving tenant: `rictl tenant move --from pool-ded-eu-west-23 --to cygnus-spare --tenant cygnus-prod-ten1` estimated ~60s for traffic drain/attachment.
incident-bot: logs (latest): `2026-03-17T12:05:10Z host=pool-ded-23 kernel: kvcache.miss_rate=0.73 seqlen.avg=1187 tenant=cygnus-prod-ten1` ; alerts tripped: cpu_high, tail_latency_surge.
sre-luca: observing immediate effect: after enabling throttle, tail latency dropped from 4.6s -> 1.6s within 90s. p99 still ~1.6s but trending down. recommend enabling prefix KV caching and keep spare attached.
eng-aya: enabling prefix caching: `rictl caching set --tenant cygnus-prod-ten1 --mode prefix --ttl 60s` — applied.
cs-emily: to Cygnus POC: "We're applying mitigations now (throttle + move + fallback). Expecting user-visible recovery in 5-10 minutes. No data deletion; only throttling and fallback applied. Will update in 5."
customer-bill: thanks. any chance payments will be reprocessed or are we dropping them? we need clarity for our ops.
cs-emily: replying -> no drops. requests either served (possibly with lower-quality responses) or rate-limited (received 429). We logged all events for replay if needed.
ops-oncall-ryan: scheduling handoff note: I'll be oncall for 25 more minutes, then hand over to @sre-luca. please keep a tight watch for 30m post-mitigation before we close warroom.
sre-ryan: post-incident checklist items: capture seq-length distribution, KV miss timeline, pool eviction logs, tenant request patterns; propose longer-term: tenant isolation policy and reserved capacity for Cygnus or stricter max-seq policy.
eng-aya: archiving logs + metrics snapshots to /incidents/7165432100/artifacts ; saved evals for model-fallback regression under `evals/7165432100/fallback-compare`.
ops-oncall-ryan: will tentatively close warroom in 40m if stable for 30m. if p99 <= 1.2s for 30m, mark as resolved and open follow-up ticket for capacity/quotas.
customer-bill: appreciate the rapid response, please keep us posted. :heart:
